reader.summary: Japan's news cycle was dominated by the historic launch of a spacecraft on a round-trip mission to Mars' moon Phobos, aiming to collect and return soil samples for the first time. On the economic front, core inflation surged to 2.1%, exceeding the Bank of Japan's target and cementing near-term rate-hike expectations, even as the BOJ signalled it might raise its inflation forecast while holding rates steady. Exports grew 16.7% in September on AI chip and auto demand, though one report framed the same figure as a 'huge miss' and a slowdown, and manufacturing PMI hit a seven-month low. PM Takaichi's approval rating slipped below 50% amid a cabinet scandal, and she publicly rejected criticism of the weak yen and high interest rates. Security saw the US ban BYD vehicles from a strategic air base, joint US-Japan drills around islands (partially disrupted by Typhoon Champi), and a Japanese journalist remaining jailed in Moscow, further eroding already fragile Russia ties. Japanese banks and airlines scrambled to patch critical PHP vulnerabilities, and a Chinese AI tool linked to Korean bank hacks was also used in Japan. China squeezed Japan on rare-earth supply and condemned Yasukuni Shrine visits. In sport, Fiji stunned Eddie Jones's Japan in rugby, and Katie Boulter reached the Japan Open semi-final.

key_events.event: Japan launched a spacecraft on a historic round-trip mission to collect and return soil samples from Mars' moon Phobos.
Japan's core inflation rose to 2.1%, exceeding the BOJ's 2% target and capping near-term rate-hike expectations.
PM Takaichi's public support fell below 50% for the first time since taking office amid a cabinet scandal.
The US military banned BYD vehicles from a strategic air base in Japan over security concerns.
A Japanese journalist remained jailed in Moscow, described as the latest sign of deteriorating Japan-Russia ties.
Typhoon Champi battered Japan and partially disrupted US-Japan joint military drills around the islands.
Japanese banks and airlines went offline scrambling to patch critical PHP vulnerabilities that roiled the global internet.
Japan's September exports rose 16.7% driven by AI chip and automotive demand, though manufacturing PMI hit a seven-month low.
China squeezed Japan's critical rare-earth supply, with Japan reportedly months from running out, and condemned Japan's 'negative moves' over Yasukuni Shrine.
Fiji defeated Eddie Jones's Japan in a rugby match, and Katie Boulter reached the Japan Open semi-final.

display.eli5:
Japan just launched a spacecraft to grab dirt from a tiny moon of Mars and bring it home. That is a world first. Next week, the spacecraft will be flying through space, and mission controllers will confirm it is on the right path. People will be excited, and scientists around the world will be comparing it to past Mars missions.

The Bank of Japan is about to hold its big policy meeting. Inflation went above their target, so everyone expects them to say they are getting ready to raise interest rates soon. That will make the yen and Japanese stocks move, and it will be a huge story in the news.

Prime Minister Takaichi is in a tricky spot. Her approval rating just dropped below 50%, there is a cabinet scandal, and she is about to hit her one-year anniversary in office. Opposition parties will be piling on, and she will have to defend her record publicly.

A surprise would be the government suddenly announcing emergency plans to secure rare-earth minerals, because China is squeezing Japan's supply and officials say Japan could run out within months. That would be a big deal for factories and tech companies.

Round 2026-10-17:
Japan's week was defined by a diplomatic shock: Russia arrested and detained a Japanese journalist in its Far East region on suspicion of espionage, prompting Tokyo to formally demand explanations and rebuke Moscow. PM Takaichi publicly denied any spying allegations, and the incident became the latest flare-up in already strained Russia-Japan relations. On the economic front, Japan committed up to twenty-one billion dollars to finance two new GlobalFoundries semiconductor plants in New York, a major bet on reshoring advanced chip production and deepening US-Japan industrial ties. The International Monetary Fund also projected India would overtake Japan as the world's fourth-largest economy by 2027, a symbolic milestone that drew broad commentary. Domestically, Takaichi's cabinet suffered its first resignation when the farm minister stepped down amid a scandal; a replacement was quickly named. Takaichi's offhand remark that household chores and makeup add hours to her workday ignited a nationwide debate about gender
